FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

In-form Real Betis look to cement their top-four position as they host strugglers Rayo Vallecano, who appear destined for a relegation battle in La Liga this term.

Match News and Current Form

Betis conceded late on to draw last weekend’s derby at Sevilla, but responded to that disappointment with a UEFA Champions League win in midweek at Slovan Bratislava (2-0), and have now lost just one of their last eight competitive games (W5, D2). The Heliopolitans will remain fourth in La Liga this weekend regardless of results, but can be confident of putting some pressure on those above them having won a joint league-high eight home matches since the start of May (L1). Boss Manuel Pellegrini’s stellar record against these opponents should offer further hope, as he’s lost just one of his last 13 H2Hs (W6, D6).

Rayo have endured a tough start to life under Beñat San José, who inherited a side that were beaten Conference League finalists but now find themselves teetering ominously above the relegation zone. Having won only one of their last six league games (D2, L3), the Red Sashes are looking to avoid losing three games on the spin in La Liga for the first time since February. Anything but a victory would see Rayo risk ending the weekend in the bottom three, but the omens are not good on that front given that they are yet to win on their travels in La Liga this term (D2, L4).  

Head-to-Head History

Betis are winless in five meetings having drawn the last four (L1), but Rayo’s last away H2H victory came back in August 2012 (D5, L4).

Win Probability
Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Betis have scored a league-high seven goals from set-pieces this term.

Betis registered over 14.5 shots in eight of their last 11 matches.

None of Rayo’s last four league games saw both teams score.

Only one side have conceded more penalties than Rayo (5) in La Liga this season.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

With his brace in midweek, Cucho Hernández has registered six goal involvements in his last seven games for Betis (G5, A1), while his last four scoring appearances in La Liga saw him net before half-time. Rayo midfielder Unai López has won just three of his 11 career H2Hs against Betis (D3, L5) and has never scored against them - he was last on target in an away match back in February 2021!

Betis appear likely to remain without Dani Ceballos and Giovani Lo Celso. Rayo remain without Augusto Batalla and Óscar Valentín among others.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Recent H2Hs have not produced an abundance of goals, so Betis to win and under 2.5 total goals looks a viable combination.

Author: Ben Olawumi
